issue.title: daemon status lists "on the network" addresses that --web isn't bound to
issue.body:
## What happens

When `magpie serve` runs with `--web` bound to one specific address, `magpie daemon status` (and the serve startup log) still lists every interface address under "on the network", even though magpie web does not listen on them.

```
$ magpie serve --web=100.x.y.z:3430      # bound to the Tailscale address only
$ magpie daemon status
  page    http://100.x.y.z:3430/?k=...
  on the network http://10.a.b.c:3430/?k=...     # VPC NIC  — not listening
  on the network http://172.17.0.1:3430/?k=...   # docker0  — not listening
```

```
$ ss -ltnp | grep 3430
LISTEN 0 4096 100.x.y.z:3430 0.0.0.0:*  users:(("magpie",...))
$ curl http://10.a.b.c:3430/     # connection refused
$ curl http://172.17.0.1:3430/   # connection refused
```

## Expected

If `--web` is bound to a specific host, list only that address (and the "on the network" lines only when bound to `0.0.0.0` / `::`). As is, the status output points at links that don't work and suggests the admin page (with its key in the URL) is exposed on interfaces where it isn't, which is confusing when checking exposure on a headless server.

## Version

magpie 0.1.1331, Ubuntu 24.04 (headless), systemd user service.

comments.body:
**Root cause** — `printDaemonWeb` (`magpie daemon status`, `magpie daemon web`, internal/cli/daemon_cli.go) and `printWeb` (the `magpie web` / `magpie serve` startup log, internal/cli/web_cli.go) listed one link per interface address of the computer whenever the page's bind host was a non-loopback IP. The branch meant for a bind to every interface took a bind to one address as well, so with `--web=100.x.y.z:3430` the status printed "on the network" links, key included, at addresses where nothing listens — as the report's `ss` and `curl` show. (The gateway's own `LANURLs` has listed a pinned `MAGPIE_ADDR` alone for a while; the page printers lacked the same distinction.)

**Fix**

- Both printers enumerate the network links only for a bind to every interface (0.0.0.0, `::`, or a host left empty in the service file). A page bound to one address is said to answer there alone: its own link (the "page" line already prints it) and the warning that anyone with the link can change magpie — which still holds at the bound address.
- A reverse proxy's link (`MAGPIE_WEB_URL`, or `MAGPIE_PUBLIC_URL` with no port, #372/#1479) is still printed for a pinned bind, so no working link is lost.
- `magpie web --addr=<ip>:port` and the serve banner get the same treatment, from the same `printWeb`.

**Verification**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| new `TestWebPrintListsTheBindAlone` (internal/cli) | red before the fix — with `MAGPIE_PUBLIC_URL` set, the pinned-bind rows of both printers printed the network link; green after; the two `0.0.0.0` rows keep the enumeration |
| the daemon/web/serve family (`TestDaemon*`, `TestWeb*`, `TestServe*`, `TestShareLines`, `TestKeyNote`, `TestAdvertisedURL`) | ok |
| `go test -count=1 -tags nogui ./internal/cli` full | ok |
| `go test -count=1 ./internal/gui` full | ok |
| `gofmt -l`, `go vet` (linux, windows, darwin without cgo) | clean |
| `go build` linux / windows (-tags nogui) | ok |

**Not verified on real hardware:** a real systemd install with `--web` on one address — the report's `ss`/`curl` evidence is taken from the report, and the printers are driven directly here. A re-run of `magpie daemon status` on the affected server is worth doing.

**Branch**: [`fix/4843-status-lists-bound-addr`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/4843-status-lists-bound-addr), head `f27d107b388001d995952e46841da37d29ace040` (on top of upstream/main `c86fa2a34`).

This is a fork branch, ready for review, not a claim on the issue's ownership.
